claims.text: Adding 5 wt% MoS2 to the CoCrFeNi matrix will form a low-friction tribofilm on the wear surface.
A binder or encapsulation method will improve the stability and durability of the MoS2 tribofilm.
MoS2 reduces friction by forming a protective tribofilm on the wear surface.
The MoS2-derived tribofilm will remain stable from room temperature to 800 °C in dry air.
The protective tribofilm will suppress the high-temperature increase in friction of CoCrFeNi.
The protective tribofilm will suppress the high-temperature increase in wear of CoCrFeNi.
Unreinforced CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increased friction and wear at high temperatures.
At 10 N in dry air, the modified material will have a coefficient of friction at least 20% lower than unreinforced CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
At 10 N in dry air, the modified material will have a wear rate at least 20% lower than unreinforced CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that the tribofilm is stable across the entire temperature range, while the uncertainty field identifies possible high-temperature degradation or removal of that same tribofilm.
